[H1] Admission
[H3] Entry Test for Engineering Programs – Fall 2026 Intake

Home
Admission
Admission
Entry Test for Engineering Programs – Fall 2026 Intake
IST doesn’t conduct its own entry test. The results of following entry tests are acceptable to apply for admission in undergraduate programs offered by IST. Applicants can appear in any one of the below mentioned tests and can use the higher score to apply for admission in IST:
NAT which is conducted by NTS in every month
HAT which is conducted by ETC-HEC
NET which is conducted by NUST Islamabad
ECAT which is conducted by UET Lahore
ETEA which is conducted by UET Peshawar
Entry Test for Engineering Programs conducted by MUET Jamshoro
Entry Test for Engineering Programs conducted by NED Karachi
ACT which is conducted by ACT-USA
Further details related to acceptable entry tests dates & categories are as under:
NAT Acceptable Test Dates & Categories
The test is conducted by NTS in all major cities of Pakistan in every month. Interested students are required to visit NTS website i.e.
https://nts.org.pk/Test&Products/Announced/05_26/NAT_GAT_May2026/index.php
or contact NTS to get desired information related to the registration procedure, test dates and centers etc.
Acceptable Dates:
The results of the NAT conducted by NTS from
July 01, 2025 to July 31, 2026
are acceptable to apply for admission in BS programs offered by IST.
Acceptable Categories:
NAT-1E and NAT-1CS, both are acceptable to apply for admission in BS Engineering Programs
HAT Acceptable Test Dates & Categories
HEC has established Education Testing Commission (ETC) to hold Higher Education Aptitude Test (HAT) for UG admissions.
Acceptable Dates:
The results of the HAT-UG tests announced/ available from
July 01, 2025 to July 31, 2026
are acceptable to apply for admission in BS programs offered by IST.
Acceptable Categories:
HAT–UG–E and HAT–UG–CS, both are acceptable to apply for admission in BS Engineering Programs
NET Acceptable Test Dates & Categories
The result of NUST Entry Test (NET) announced/ available from
December, 2025 to July 31, 2026
are acceptable to apply for admission in BS programs offered by IST.
Acceptable Categories:
NET (Engineering Category), NET (Computer Science) both are acceptable to apply for admission in all BS Engineering Programs
ECAT Acceptable Test Date & Category
The result of ECAT conducted by University of Engineering & Technology (UET) Lahore for
Fall 2026 intake
in Engineering Programs announced/ available before last date of admissions announced by IST will be acceptable to apply for admission in all BS Engineering Programs offered by IST.
ETEA Acceptable Test Date & Category
The result of ETEA conducted by University of Engineering & Technology (UET) Peshawar for
Fall 2026
intake in Engineering Programs announced/ available before last date of admissions announced by IST will be acceptable to apply for admission in all BS Engineering Programs offered by IST.
MUET Jamshoro Acceptable Test Date & Category
The result of Entry Test conducted by Mehran University of Engineering & Technology (MUET), Jamshoro for
Fall 2026
intake in Engineering Programs announced/ available before last date of admissions announced by IST will be acceptable to apply for admission in all BS Engineering Programs offered by IST.
NED UET Acceptable Test Date & Category
The result of Entry Test conducted by NED University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi for
Fall 2026
intake in Engineering Programs announced/ available before last date of admissions announced by IST will be acceptable to apply for admission in all BS Engineering Programs offered by IST.
ACT Acceptable Test Dates
The composite score of ACT conducted from
July 01, 2025 to July 31, 2026
is acceptable to apply for admission in BS programs offered by IST. Candidates are required to enter their ACT Composite Score in their online application form and upload the score card available in “MyACT account” otherwise their application will not be processed.

Disclaimer:

Registration
Before the commencement of classes of each semester, all active students are registered for courses offered by respective department. A student shall not be considered to have been registered for the semester unless all previous dues have been paid.
Hostel accommodation and transport facilities shall only be provided to students after registration.
Every student must update his/her personal information shown in student portal at the start of every semester.
Fine for Late Payment
The following fine will be levied for payment of fee after due date:
For first fifteen days after the due date, 5% of the total payable amount
After fifteen days and up to one month after due date, 10% of the total payable amount
Students will only be allowed to appear in final exam after deposit of outstanding dues along with fine
Mode of Payment
Payment of fees can be made through online Transfer/Bank Draft/Pay order against the fee challan issued at any online branch of Meezan Bank (Nationwide).
Note
: Cheques and Cash are not acceptable.

Disclaimer:

Registration
Before the commencement of classes of each semester, all active students are registered for courses offered by respective department. A student shall not be considered to have been registered for the semester unless all previous dues have been paid.
Hostel accommodation and transport facilities shall only be provided to students after registration.
Every student must update his/her personal information shown in student portal at the start of every semester.
Fine for Late Payment
The following fine will be levied for payment of fee after due date:
For first fifteen days after the due date, 5% of the total payable amount
After fifteen days and up to one month after due date, 10% of the total payable amount
Students will only be allowed to appear in final exam after deposit of outstanding dues along with fine
Mode of Payment
Payment of fees can be made through online Transfer/Bank Draft/Pay order against the fee challan issued at any online branch of Meezan Bank (Nationwide).
Note
: Cheques and Cash are not acceptable.

For first fifteen days after the due date, 5% of the total payable amount
After fifteen days and up to one month after due date, 10% of the total payable amount
Students will only be allowed to appear in final exam after deposit of outstanding dues along with fine
Mode of Payment
Payment of fees can be made through online Transfer/Bank Draft/Pay order against the fee challan issued at any online branch of HBL (Nationwide).
Note
: Cheques and Cash are not acceptable.

Sponsorship for BS Students
Several elite National Research & Development (R&D) organizations provide sponsorships to the deserving BS students of selected programs after test/interview. The sponsorship covers tuition fee and a guaranteed job after graduation, provided all requirements of the sponsoring organization are fulfilled by the candidate.
Merit Scholarships for BS Students
IST offers merit scholarships to three students (excluding sponsored students) in each discipline as per the existing policy. Scholarships are granted on the basis of admissions merit and semester results.
Below mentioned criteria shall be followed for the award of merit scholarships to BS students of each batch of each undergraduate program offered by IST:-
FOR FIRST SEMESTER:
Ser.
Scholarship Type
Merit Position
Tuition Fee Waiver

IST-1

FOR SUBSEQUENT SEMESTERS:
Ser.
Scholarship Type
Merit Position
Tuition Fee Waiver
Minimum Criteria
01
IST-1
1st
100 %
SGPA > 3.50
02
IST-2
2nd
50 %
SGPA > 3.50
03
IST-3
3rd
25 %
SGPA > 3.50
GENERAL CONDITIONS:
Full time students with full load of studies in a regular semester will qualify for the award of Merit Scholarship.
Merit/ position for the scholarships will be based on SGPA. However, both SGPA and CGPA will be considered to ascertain the eligibility of the student for Scholarship.
Students getting any type of scholarships/ sponsored by any organization are not eligible for merit scholarship.
Student will be awarded only one scholarship (merit or need based) from IST’s own funds (whichever is higher) at a time.
In case of two or more students securing the same merit position (Admissions’ Merit Position/ same SGPA and CGPA), allocated amounts of respective scholarships for these positions shall be equally distributed among them.
If students ‘A’ & ‘B’ jointly declared at 1st position, then the student ‘C’ would be at 3rd position and so on.
No scholarship shall be awarded if there is an ‘I’ Grade in preceding semester.
No scholarship shall be awarded if there is a ‘W’ Grade in preceding semester.
Student should take full load of credit hours in that preceding semester.
In case, a student takes any additional/ repeat course(s), his/ her merit position will be calculated on the basis of normal load of credit hours in that semester.
In case of semester freeze, merit scholarship would only be awarded after re-joining of the student.
Transferred students shall not be eligible for the award of merit scholarship on the basis of results of courses which they studied with the students of previous department/ program. However, such students shall be reconsidered for merit scholarship on the basis of results of courses which they will study with the students of their new department/ program.
In situations where existing rules & regulations are found silent/unavailable, the decision made by IST will be the final which can’t be challenged anywhere.
The contents as stated in merit scholarship policy are expression of intent only. The institute reserves the right to discontinue any portion or make amendments in merit scholarship policy/ rules & regulations at any time without notice.

EHSAAS Scholarships for BS Students
Higher Education Commission (HEC) with the support of Government of Pakistan has launched “EHSAAS Undergraduate Scholarship Project” for the qualified students from low income families to complete undergraduate studies (Four-Five-year Bachelor programs) from public sector Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) of Pakistan, Azad Jammu & Kashmir, and Gilgit Baltistan. The principle objective of the EHSAAS Undergraduate Project is to provide assistance to the maximum number of students who have secured admission to the universities in various disciplines but lack of financial means to continue their studies. The needy students admitted in IST are informed to apply for EHSAAS Scholarship as and when announced by HEC.
HEC Need Based Scholarships for BS Students
Pakistan has no shortage of talented youth, but in several instances, lack of resources prevents them from realizing their potentials. This becomes more problematic when it comes to accessing higher education. The Government of Pakistan acknowledges these constraints and has tasked Higher Education Commission to facilitate the needy and deserving students through Need Based Scholarships. Scholarships are announced for financially disadvantaged students of as many as 94 public sector universities and their campuses. The needy students admitted in IST are informed to apply for HEC Need Based Scholarship after the completion of admission process subject to availability of funds/seats.
The Punjab Educational Endowment Fund (PEEF)
The Punjab Educational Endowment Fund (PEEF) under guidance of the Board of Directors is providing opportunities to the talented but needy students to fulfill their dreams and aspirations and at the same time to become partner in the development and welfare of Pakistan. The PEEF, since its inception in 2009 has awarded more than 374,000 scholarships to students of Punjab and other provinces which are currently pursuing education through public and private sector institutions. Needy students, admitted in IST, can also apply for this scholarship. The details are available at
https://www.peef.org.pk/Scholarships_Main.html
Loans
Interest free loans are also provided to IST students by National Bank of Pakistan (NBP). The process to apply for loan and other details are available at
https://www.nbp.com.pk/studentloan/

Al Khwarizmi Scholarships for Foreign Students
Scholarships are available for Foreign Students to study in Bachelor/ Master/ Doctoral Degree Programs offered by IST.
Duration of Scholarship:
For BS (Bachelor’s) Students: Upto 04 years
For MS (Master’s) Students: Upto 2.5 years
For PhD (Doctoral) Students: Upto 04 years
The scholarship program covers funds for the following expenses:
University tuition fee as per actual
Stipend @ PKR 15000, 20000 & 35000 per month for students admitted in BS, MS & PhD programs respectively
Stipend @ PKR 50000 per month for scientist/ post doc fellow
One time return air ticket
Mandatory academic & non-academic charges like admission fee, endowment fund, library development fund, service charges, safe/ smart campus charges, hostel charges etc. are not covered.
Admission of Foreign Applicants in IST
Click to enlarge
Admission Pre-requisites
Candidates willing to apply for admission in BS, MS/ PhD programs offered by IST must:
meet the eligibility requirements (
BS
,
MS
,
PhD
) for respective program as mentioned on IST website
be able/ willing to pay the semester dues/ allied charges as per fee structure (
BS
,
MS, PhD
) given on IST website for foreign Students. All fees and other charges are subject to revision from time to time
be proficient in English as all educational and extracurricular activities such as "Class Lectures, Oral and Written Examinations, Quizzes, Assignments, Seminars, Conferences, Notifications etc" at Institute of Space Technology (IST) Islamabad take place in English Language
obtain equivalence certificate from
IBCC
/
HEC
, Pakistan (keeping in view the eligibility requirements to apply for respective program) before the closing date of application to apply for admission in IST. In case any document proves to be false, fake, or fabricated at a later stage, a provisionally admitted student shall be liable to expulsion from the University at any stage or to any other disciplinary or legal action the University may deem necessary
obtain No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their Ministry of Foreign Affairs or their Embassy in Pakistan
prepare personal statement, in English, should include self-introduction, study and work experience, reasons for application and study plan/ research proposal
obtain two letters of recommendation from full professors or associate professors, in English. (Professors’ signature, contact phone number and email address must be put on the letter)
be willing to meet/ abide all requirements/ rules & regulations issued by the IST/ HEC/ Concerned Government Organizations/ Departments from time to time
possess adequate mental and physical health to continue his/ her course of studies
Procedure
Admissions will be announced by IST in national newspapers/ on IST website
Foreign applicants meeting the pre-requisites will be required to apply online at IST’s website www.ist.edu.pk
Foreign applicants will be required to complete online application form in all respects including the deposit/ online transfer of application processing fee before the last date to apply for admission in IST for further process
Merit of foreign applicants will be determined according the merit determination criteria mentioned on IST website
Merit lists of provisionally selected BS and MS candidates shall be displayed on IST website whereas, provisionally selected PhD candidates will be intimated through email
Provisionally selected BS, MS & PhD candidates will deposit admission dues as per details shared by IST to secure their seat
Cases of selected foreign applicants for provisional admission in IST will be referred to Higher Education Commission (HEC) and relevant Government department(s) along with their passport copy, photographs, admission letter, NoC of their Embassy/ Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Student’s Information Sheet for Issuance of No Objection Certificate (NoC)/ final approval as per the
policy
in vogue
Selected foreign applicants for provisional admission in IST will be required to approach the Pakistani mission abroad for the visa and submits the following documents:
Application Form (Student Visa Form)
Photocopy of Passport
Photograph
Educational Documents
Admission Letter of University
No Objection Certificate (NOC) issued by the Home Country to Study in Pakistan
Any other document if required by Pakistan Embassy at respective country
Joining instructions will be issued to the provisionally selected foreign applicants after:
The completion of all admission requirements of IST
Receiving the intimation/ NOC from HEC/ Concerned Government Organizations
Successfully joined foreign applicants/ students will be required to meet/ abide all requirements/ rules & regulations issued by the IST/ HEC/ Concerned Government Organizations/ Departments from time to time
IST reserves the right to make amendments in the policy regarding the admission of foreign students at any time without notice/ cancel or refuse admission to any foreign applicant at any time/ stage without assigning any reason
Contact Details
Incharge Admissions
Focal Person (International Student Office)
Email:
admissions@ist.edu.pk
Contact: +92-51-9075100

Notes
Applicants with ICS (Math, Physics & Computer Science) qualification are allowed to apply for all BS engineering programs offered by IST. However, such candidates will be required to study Chemistry as a remedial subject/ course in the 1st semester after admission.
A-Level / Cambridge/ Students with any qualification other than FSC/ ICS/ DAE are required obtain equivalent certificate from IBCC according to the eligibility criteria of respective program.
Pre-medical students with additional math or appearing for additional math papers this year are eligible to apply in related programs as per eligibility criteria.
Candidates with HSSC Pre-Medical backgrounds can now apply for all engineering programs after completing an 8-week condensed Mathematics course from a recognized university.
HSSC/ A-Level/ Equivalent final result awaiting students of “first annual exams only” are eligible to apply. Such applicants, if selected on merit, will be offered provisional admission and they will be required to submit the HSSC Result Card/ Equivalent Certificate (according to the eligibility requirements of respective program) issued by IBCC in Admissions Office before the start of first semester exams/ within 15 days after the announcement of results (whichever is earlier).
DAE (3 Years) students possessing complete/ final DAE result are eligible to apply in related programs as per eligibility criteria.
International applicants are also required to fulfill other requirements laid down by the Higher Education Commission (HEC) for the admission of international students in Pakistani Higher Education Institutions/ Universities.
In accordance with normal policy in admission matters, the completion of admission requirements within due date shall be the sole responsibility of the student, and non-compliance with the requirements shall result in termination of the admission at the risk and cost of the student.
The institute reserves the right to discontinue any portion or make amendments in General Eligibility Criteria at any time without notice.
It is the responsibility of the candidate/ applicant to provide the required academic record/ certificates in time to the University, as per the deadline.
The University reserves the right to drop any program, if number of candidates are less than the sufficient number to offer the program.

Steps of Enrollment in MS & PhD Programs offered by IST
Step 1 - Admissions Announcement on IST Website/ National Newspapers
Graduate (MS & PhD) admissions are announced on IST Website/ National Newspapers twice a year i.e. in April/ May & November/ December.
Step 2 - Completion of Online Admission Form
Candidates interested to apply for admission in IST are required to visit
www.ist.edu.pk
or
https://eportal.ist.edu.pk/
to create an online account, read & understand the eligibility & merit determination criteria, fee structure, fee refund policy and other related information. Subsequently, eligible candidates willing to apply for admission in IST are required to complete online admission form by providing desired information and uploading the scan copies of required documents with online admission form.
Step 3 - Deposit of Application Processing Fee
After creating an online account, applicants are required to download the challan form available at online admission form to deposit of application processing fee (non-refundable) in any online branch of HBL (within due date).
It is a mandatory requirement.
An email is sent for the confirmation of receipt of application processing fee and in parallel; fee receipt status is also updated at online admission form. In case if the application processing fee status is not updated at online admission within one week after the deposit of application processing fee then such applicants are required to contact Admissions Office with proof through email.
Step 4 - Merit Lists/ Admissions Status
MS Applicants are required to check their admission status on IST website by using the login details. An email/ SMS is also sent to provisionally selected applicants. However, applicants are strongly advised to keep visiting the IST website for updated information.
PhD applicants recommended by the concerned academic department are intimated by Admissions Office through email/ telephone call.
Step 5 – Acceptance of Admission
Provisionally selected applicants in respective programs are required to download the admission package by accessing the online admission system preferably through IST website. Admission package contain the offer letter, fee challan form/s, an affidavit (write-up), fee refund policy and other documents required to be submitted for registration in IST.
Step 6 – Reservation of Seat to avail Hostel/ Transport Facility (optional)
After the acceptance of admission offer, on the same page of online admission system, candidates are required to reserve hostel /transport seat (
if they want to avail services of IST otherwise skip this section
). Transport facility is provided only to the students of Rawalpindi & Islamabad from the designated points. IST have within campus separate hostel facility for male and female students with limited capacity therefore interested applicants can avail hostel facility subject to availability of seats.
Step 7 – Deposit of Fee
Candidates fulfilling the admissions requirements and willing to join IST are required to deposit the fee in any online branch of HBL within due date mentioned on challan forms. An email/ SMS is also sent for the confirmation of receipt of fee.
It is highlighted that fully automated admission system of IST does not allow a late fee option. Therefore, nonpayment of dues within due date will make you in-eligible for admission in IST.
Step 8 – Welcome to IST on Registration Day
Provisionally admitted students are required to prepare the documents according to Offer Letter for the submission on Registration Day.

Steps of Enrollment in BS Programs offered by IST
Step 1 - Admissions Announcement on IST Website/ National Newspapers
Undergraduate (BS) admissions are announced on IST Website/ National Newspapers once a year i.e. in March/April.
Step 2 - Completion of Online Admission Form
Candidates interested to apply for admission in IST are required to visit
www.ist.edu.pk
or
https://eportal.ist.edu.pk/
to create an online account, read & understand the eligibility & merit determination criteria, fee structure, fee refund policy and other related information. Subsequently, eligible candidates willing to apply for admission in IST are required to complete online admission form by providing desired information and uploading the scan copies of required documents with online admission form.
Step 3 - Deposit of Application Processing Fee
After creating an online account, applicants are required to download the challan form available at online admission form to deposit of application processing fee (non-refundable) in any online branch of Meezan Bank/HBL (within due date).
It is a mandatory requirement.
An email is sent for the confirmation of receipt of application processing fee and in parallel; fee receipt status is also updated at online admission form. In case if the application processing fee status is not updated at online admission within one week after the deposit of application processing fee then such applicants are required to contact Admissions Office with proof through email.
Step 4 - Merit Lists/ Admissions Status
Applicants are required to check their admission status on IST website by using the login details. An email/ SMS is also sent to provisionally selected applicants. However, applicants are strongly advised to keep visiting the IST website for updated information.
Step 5 – Acceptance of Admission
Provisionally selected applicants in respective programs are required to download the admission package by accessing the online admission system preferably through IST website. Admission package contain the offer letter, fee challan form/s, an affidavit (write-up), fee refund policy and other documents required to be submitted for registration in IST.
Step 6 – Reservation of Seat to avail Hostel/ Transport Facility (optional)
After the acceptance of admission offer, on the same page of online admission system, candidates are required to reserve hostel /transport seat (
if they want to avail services of IST otherwise skip this section
). Transport facility is provided only to the students of Rawalpindi & Islamabad from the designated points. IST have within campus separate hostel facility for male and female students with limited capacity therefore interested applicants can avail hostel facility subject to availability of seats.
Step 7 – Deposit of Fee
Candidates fulfilling the admissions requirements and willing to join IST are required to deposit the fee in any online branch of Meezan Bank/HBL within due date mentioned on challan forms. An email/ SMS is also sent for the confirmation of receipt of fee.
It is highlighted that fully automated admission system of IST does not allow a late fee option. Therefore, nonpayment of dues within due date will make you in-eligible for admission in IST and consideration in subsequent merit lists and no request is entertained in this regard.
Step 8 – Welcome to IST on Registration Day
Provisionally admitted students are required to prepare the documents according to Offer Letter for the submission on Registration Day.

[H1] Admission

Home
Admission
Admission
Space is considered to be the final frontier and world’s best minds take up the most daunting challenges to conquer it.
Fazeel Mahmood Khan, PhD
The Institute of Space Technology (IST) is a premier institution in Pakistan, renowned for its focus on space and related sciences. Here's why IST stands out:
Why Choose IST?
1. Specialized Education:
IST offers specialized education in space and related sciences, equipping students to address national and global issues.
2. Research Opportunities:
The institute has state-of-the-art research labs, providing students with hands-on experience and opportunities to contribute to cutting-edge research.
3. Accreditation and Recognition:
IST is federally chartered, HEC recognized, and PEC accredited, ensuring its degrees are valued globally.
4. Industry Connections:
IST has strong industry connections, facilitating internships, placements, and job opportunities for its graduates.
5. Student Life:
The institute offers a vibrant student life, with various societies, clubs, and sports activities, fostering personal growth and development.
6. Scholarships and Sponsorships:
IST offers merit-based scholarships and sponsorships, making quality education accessible to deserving students.
7. Global Recognition:
IST's programs are accredited under Level-II by Pakistan Engineering Council (PEC), substantially equivalent to Washington Accord, enabling graduates to work globally.
Unique Achievements
1. Satellite Development:
IST has successfully developed and launched satellites, including iCUBE1 and ICUBE-Qamar, demonstrating its expertise in space technology.
2. Research and Innovation:
The institute is committed to research and innovation, with a strong focus on solving real-world problems.
Career Opportunities
At the IST, we empower students to pursue their passion for space science and technology. Since 2002, we've been producing professionals who meet the demands of national organizations and contribute to the nation's technological advancements.
Thriving Careers Ahead
Our graduates enjoy excellent career prospects, both locally and globally. They're employed in leading organizations, including:
• Space agencies (SUPARCO, European Space Agencies)
• Aviation industry (Airbus, Emirates, Air Blue)
• Research institutes (R&D, academia)
• Government organizations (PTA, WAPDA, EPA)
• Private sector (mobile communication, agriculture, airlines)
Diverse Employment Opportunities
Our multidisciplinary approach opens doors to various industries, contributing to socioeconomic activities nationwide. Our graduates work in:
• Space science and technology
• Aerospace engineering
• Research and development
• Telecommunications
• Meteorology
• Agriculture and food sector
Global Recognition
IST graduates are recognized globally, with opportunities to pursue further education at renowned universities worldwide.
If you're passionate about space science and technology, IST is the perfect platform to launch your career. With our strong industry connections, research opportunities, and global recognition, you'll be well-equipped to succeed in your chosen field.

IST Alumni Spotlight – Stars That Shine Beyond Boundaries
We are excited to launch a new series that celebrates the incredible journeys of our brilliant alumni — individuals who began their journeys at the
Institute of Space Technology (IST)
and went on to make remarkable contributions across industries and around the world.
From space science to entrepreneurship, research labs to boardrooms, IST graduates continue to inspire with their innovation, resilience, and impact.
This series,
"IST Alumni Spotlight – Stars That Shine Beyond Boundaries"
is our tribute to their achievements. Through personal stories, career milestones, and bold transitions, we aim to highlight how our alumni are shaping the future — in ways both expected and extraordinary.
Kicking off the series:
Amina Malik
- Aerospace Major - Class of 2006 A successful Aerospace Engineer turned entrepreneur, Amina’s story is one of reinvention, courage, and cross - industry innovation. From Airbus to her own brand NAURÉ, she exemplifies the spirit of IST — bold, visionary, and ever-evolving.
Stay Tuned

Facilities at IST
Overview
Going to IST is about making the most of your life as a student. As you get involved, you'll not only have a lot of fun, you'll also develop your leadership abilities, raise your consciousness, and acquire skills you'll use after graduation. Together students, faculty and staff of IST create a welcoming and enterprising community to achieve all this.
List of student societies is always evolving with the changing interests of students. Are you interested in academics, athletics, socializing, social work, performing arts, gaming or movies? There's a good chance that a student society exists for what you want to do.
Wellness and Counseling Center
Wellness and Counseling Center, IST
is dedicated to help students, faculty and staff members maximize their sense of overall well-being and facilitate them towards making healthy contributions to their academic, personal, social and career development.
The Centre provides
free and confidential on- campus
psychological counseling services, both in individual or group settings, where the students address their concerns with a highly trained mental health clinician in a safe and non-judgmental environment.
The Centre further aims to highlight social stigma and spread awareness regarding various topics of mental health through workshops, advocacy and outreach programs.
For your convenience, there are many ways to
book a counseling appointment
for your professional and personal concerns with either a male or a female therapist,
You can
email
our psychologists directly at
annum.tanweer@ist.edu.pk
or
taj.iqbal@ist.edu.pk
You can
call
directly at 051-9075859 between 9 a.m to 12 p.m - Monday to Friday.
You can
visit
Department of Humanities and Sciences, IST or Wellness and Counseling Center at Second Floor, Rashid Block, IST.
Housing & Dining
Hostel Registration Form
Boarding Facility
Boarding facilities will be limited to students living outside Rawalpindi / Islamabad area. IST is managing 03 x hostels for boys and 1 x hostel for girls. Students are expected to bring decent colour linen and their amenities with them at the time of joining. Boarding facility will only be given depending on availability of rooms.
Cafeteria Services
The cafeteria services in IST are provioded by Cafeteria Contractor on cash basis. A spcious and well managed cafeteria is available on campus. However, cafeteria services in outside hostels are provided by Cafeteria Contractor(s) and Owner of Girls Hostel for girls, on fixed monthly basis.
Tuck Shop Services
A well-organized Tuck Shop is available on campus which caters students’ needs and serves all kind of beverages and snacks etc.
Dining Timings
Dining timings at IST and outside hostels are as under:-
Working Days
Breakfast - 0700 hrs to 0800 hrs
Lunch - 1130 hrs to 1500 hrs
Dinner - 2000 hrs to 2230 hrs
Weekends / Holidays
Breakfast - 0730 hrs to 1000 hrs
Lunch - 1330 hrs to 1430 hrs
Dinner - 2030 hrs to 2230 hrs
Quality Assurance Committees
A committee headed by a senior Administration member, Representatives of faculty, administration and students is constituted to check / cater the standard / quality of Cafeteria Services on campus and outside hostels.
Laundry Facility
Laundry facility is available at IST campus which caters the washing and ironing requirements of all boarding students. Fixed charges of laundry shop are paid by students on semester basis.
Attendant Services
One attendant in each wing of the hostel would be available for cleaning of rooms and other minor chores. The charges of the attendant will be born by students themselves.
Health & Safety
IST Safety Department is responsible for developing and maintaining a safe and secure environment for the employees and students so that they can pursue their academic, professional and personal ambitions. Committed to serving with professional excellence, we strive to be approachable, reliable and truly service-oriented in the performance of our duties. The department maintains strong, professional relationships with all stake holders to ensure continuous collaboration on emergency planning efforts and familiarity with our campus in the event of an emergency.
The following facilities are available at IST for Safety of individuals and premises during emergency.
Fire Safety Facilities
All buildings of IST have dedicated Emergency Exits and are also equipped with fire extinguishers, Water Hydrants. In addition, some areas e.g. data center are equipped with latest firefighting system (FM-200), smoke and heat detectors.
IST also has an in-house, highly trained firefighting team that is equipped with latest Fire Tenders and other modern firefighting equipment.
Health Facilities
Health care is an important and necessary part of any organization. The true mark of an organization is how it looks after its employees and others.
Institute of Space Technology provides medical cover to its employees and students. Medical cover consists of Professional man-power, MI Room, First Aid Facility, Ambulance for 24 hours and First Aid boxes at different locations. The employees of Institute and their families are entitled to free medical treatment from panel hospitals.
IST is providing necessary Information, Instructions and training regarding Health, Safety and Environment to all at IST Campus.

[H1] National Centers
[H2] National Center for Failure Analysis (NCFA)

(Live page: https://ist.edu.pk/national-centers — original path returns 404 on new site.)

Home National Centers National Centers National Centers Home National Center for Failure Analysis (NCFA) Institute of Space Technology (IST), following its vision of establishing state of the art Centers of Excellence which would chart a path across all the academic departments/programs of our institute, established Failure Analysis Center (FAC) in March 2013, which has now been upgraded to a national level facility “National Center for Failure Analysis (NCFA)”. NCFA will not only provide a place for research to all the faculty and PhD/MS scholars, but will also be a resource for providing solutions of materials related services to local industries. This initiative is expected to fill a large void, as services being offered at NCFA are currently not available in the country under a single umbrella. It would support a variety of industries by conducting Material Analysis (MA), Failure Analysis (FA), Structural Integrity Assessment (SIA) and providing Material & Process Advisory Services (MPAS). The facility, while still in its infancy, has already commenced to provide consultancy in the following areas: Failure Analysis of metal parts/components/systems by applying “Root Cause Approach” with the aim to ensure avoidance of similar recurrences. Provision of advisory, services or both to the desirous manufactures for: Identifying/selecting metals & processes (including alternative solutions) essentially required for developing parts/components either afresh or through reverse engineering. Inspection of raw materials, on site processing of materials (including heat & surface treatments) and the finished items. Estimation of the status of parts/components/systems with view to: Recommend necessary measures for their restoration (if required & possible). Determine the remaining “safe life period”, for their operational usage. Establish inspection criterion & intervals for parts/components/systems during their “safe life period”. Training of Human Resource: Through formal programs at IST. On-site training on need basis. In order to provide above stated services/advisory, NCFA has opted to follow modern trends being practiced worldwide in relevant fields/domains. This approach entails: Only essentially required “state-of- the- art” facilities be established in house. A strong pragmatic collaborative network comprising those organizations which already have some authenticated facilities be formed for gaining benefits of their expertise in specific areas and lowering the operational costs. A vibrant advisory board of domain experts (regardless of their geographical locations) be formed for sharing & exchanging experiences Organizations must remain connected & engaged with international community of practitioners & regulators of the domain, for remaining abreast with technological & conceptual developments NCFA plans to enhance the scope of its advisory/services gradually in a phased manner.

Home Academics Academics Home / Academics / Degrees & Programs Degrees & Programs European Aircraft License Intro The Aviation Center at Institute of Space Technology is offering internationally recognized academic program Aircraft Maintenance Engineering (AME) License with specialization in the fields of Aerospace (B1.1 & B1.2) and Avionics (B2). CATEGORY B 1 AEROSPACE Is mechanically oriented and covers aircraft structure air frame systems, engines and propellers, or rotors as appropriate. CATEGORY B 2 AVIONICS To cover electrical power and distribution and control and indication systems. Is avionics based and confers privileges similar to those of the aerospace engineer associated with avionics systems. Course Outline Aircraft Maintenance Engineering License (AMEL) Curriculum Specialization: B1 (Aerospace) B 1.1Turbine Engine Aero plane Year 1 Code Subject M1 Mathematics M2 Physics M3 Electrical Fundamentals M4 Electronic Fundamentals for Aerospace(B1) M5 Digital Techniques for Aerospace(B1) M6 Materials and Hardware M8 Basic Aerodynamics M9 Human Factors M17 Propellor Code Subject M7 Maintenance Practices M10 Aviation Legislation M15 Gas Turbine Engine M11 Turbine Aero plane Aerodynamics Structures and Systems Aircraft Maintenance Engineering License (AMEL) Curriculum Specialization: B2 (Avionics) Code Subject M1 Mathematics M2 Physics M3 Electrical Fundamentals M4 Electronic Fundamentals for Avionics (B2) M5 Digital Techniques for Avionics (B2) M6 Materials and hardware M8 Basic Aerodynamics M9 Human Factors Code Subject M7 Maintenance Practices M10 Aviation Legislation M13 Aero plane Aerodynamics Structures and Systems M14 Propulsion Eligibility Program: For SSC/FSc Students: SSC/ O-Level (with Physics & Mathematics) FSc/ A-Level (with Physics & Mathematics) 60% marks in Physics & Mathematics 60% marks in entry test Minimum Age Limit : 17 Years Fee Structure Admission Fee 150,000/- (One Time Payable at the time of Admission ) Per Paper Fee € 115/- (Pay before one month of Each Exam) OJT Fee Per Month 8,000/- Semester Fee: (Total 6 Semesters) Per Semester Fee (4 Months) 140,000/-

[H1] National Centers
[H2] National Center for Failure Analysis (NCFA)

Home
National Centers
National Centers
National Center for Failure Analysis (NCFA)
Institute of Space Technology (IST), following its vision of establishing state of the art Centers of Excellence which would chart a path across all the academic departments/programs of our institute, established Failure Analysis Center (FAC) in March 2013, which has now been upgraded to a national level facility “National Center for Failure Analysis (NCFA)”. NCFA will not only provide a place for research to all the faculty and PhD/MS scholars, but will also be a resource for providing solutions of materials related services to local industries. This initiative is expected to fill a large void, as services being offered at NCFA are currently not available in the country under a single umbrella. It would support a variety of industries by conducting Material Analysis (MA), Failure Analysis (FA), Structural Integrity Assessment (SIA) and providing Material & Process Advisory Services (MPAS). The facility, while still in its infancy, has already commenced to provide consultancy in the following areas:
Failure Analysis of metal parts/components/systems by applying “Root Cause Approach” with the aim to ensure avoidance of similar recurrences.
Provision of advisory, services or both to the desirous manufactures for:
Identifying/selecting metals & processes (including alternative solutions) essentially required for developing parts/components either afresh or through reverse engineering.
Inspection of raw materials, on site processing of materials (including heat & surface treatments) and the finished items.
Estimation of the status of parts/components/systems with view to:
Recommend necessary measures for their restoration (if required & possible).
Determine the remaining “safe life period”, for their operational usage.
Establish inspection criterion & intervals for parts/components/systems during their “safe life period”.
Training of Human Resource:
Through formal programs at IST.
On-site training on need basis.
In order to provide above stated services/advisory, NCFA has opted to follow modern trends being practiced worldwide in relevant fields/domains. This approach entails:
Only essentially required “state-of- the- art” facilities be established in house.
A strong pragmatic collaborative network comprising those organizations which already have some authenticated facilities be formed for gaining benefits of their expertise in specific areas and lowering the operational costs.
A vibrant advisory board of domain experts (regardless of their geographical locations) be formed for sharing & exchanging experiences
Organizations must remain connected & engaged with international community of practitioners & regulators of the domain, for remaining abreast with technological & conceptual developments
NCFA plans to enhance the scope of its advisory/services gradually in a phased manner.

International Astronautical Federation
September 19, 2025
2025 IAF Wrold Space Award given to Chang'E6 Lunar Mission including ICUBE-Q
Every year
IAF (International Astronautical Federation)
gives two World Space Awards. One in individual category and one in team category. In 2023 Elon Musk got the award in individual category and
James Webb Space Telescope team (from NASA CSA and ESA) team
category.
This year 2025 IAF Space Award in team category has been awarded to Chang'E-6 Lunar team that includes all Payloads (including our ICUBE-Q). Award ceremony will be held during annual IAC in Sydney Australia.

News
October 8, 2025
Dr. Ausima Sultan Malik, Assistant Professor, Department of Humanities & Sciences, delivered a talk at National University of Modern Languages on October 8, 2025, on the topic “Gendered Voices: Exploring Language, Power, and Identity in Sociolinguistics"
Dr. Ausima Sultan Malik, Assistant Professor, Department of Humanities & Sciences, delivered a talk at National University of Modern Languages on October 8, 2025, on the topic
“Gendered Voices: Exploring Language, Power, and Identity in Sociolinguistics.”
The session went beyond theoretical discussion, focusing on how language subtly shapes everyday experiences. It highlighted the ways in which word choices, silences, and patterns of speech reflect underlying structures of power, identity, and gender often in ways that remain unnoticed.
The event was particularly enriched by the active engagement of the participants. Their insightful questions, personal reflections, and willingness to reconsider familiar linguistic practices through new perspectives made the session especially meaningful. Such interactions reaffirm Dr. Ausima’s continued commitment to research, teaching, and critical dialogue in the field of sociolinguistics.

Pakistan English Conference
November 27, 2025
Faculty Participation in the Pakistan English Conference - 2025
Ms. Qurat-ul-Ain
and
Ms. Ifrah Jamil
, lecturers Humanities and Sciences Department, attended the
Pakistan English Conference titled
“Rethinking English Studies in the Global South”,
at
Government College University, Lahore
on November 27, 2025.
During the conference, Ms. Qurat-ul-Ain and Ms. Ifrah Jamil presented their research paper titled
“Teaching Undergraduate Students: A Methodological Shift from Pedagogical to Andragogical Approach”
and highlighted the evolving needs of undergraduate learners and emphasized the importance of adopting andragogical strategies to enhance student engagement and learning outcomes.
Their participation contributed to the ongoing academic dialogue on the future of English studies in the region and provided valuable representation for the Institute of Space Technology at a national academic forum

ICAST
November 18, 2025
The International Conference on Applications of Space Science and Technology (ICAST)
The International Conference on Applications of Space Science and Technology (ICAST) marks a transformative milestone in Pakistan's journey through space science and technology. As the largest space event in the country, ICAST unites the legacies of IST’s International Conference on Aerospace Science and Engineering (ICASE) and SUPARCO’s International Conference on Space (ICS) into a biennial global forum of unparalleled excellence. ICAST bringing together visionaries, global thought leaders, pioneering researchers, and industry trailblazers, aspires to redefine the future of space science by fostering collaboration, presenting transformative research, and exploring interdisciplinary space applications with the potential to reshape our collective future.

CATEGORY B 1 AEROSPACE Is mechanically oriented and covers aircraft structure air frame systems, engines and propellers, or rotors as appropriate. CATEGORY B 2 AVIONICS To cover electrical power and distribution and control and indication systems. Is avionics based and confers privileges similar to those of the aerospace engineer associated with avionics systems. [H1] Quality Enhancement
[H2] Quality Enhancement Cell - Institute of Space Technology, Islamabad

Home
Quality Enhancement
Quality Enhancement
Quality Enhancement Cell - Institute of Space Technology, Islamabad
During recent years, the realization of need for quality assurance in higher education has become a global phenomenon. Pakistan also felt the need to assess and improve the quality of higher education with the objectives of achieving international competitiveness and compatibility of our academic programs and research quality.
Quality Assurance is the means through which an institution can guarantee with confidence and certainty, that the standards of its educational provision are being maintained and enhanced.
Quality enhancement is taking deliberate steps to bring about continual improvement in the effectiveness of the learning experience of students. In QE there is greater emphasis on Internal QA and the encouragement of an institutional “Quality Culture.”
Developing an internal quality assurance mechanism in every institution is highly important. This acts as a sustainable base for External Quality Monitoring. Self Assessment, being one of the tools used for achieving Quality Assurance is conducted by the institution itself. It is meant to assess whether the existing programs are able to meet the educational objectives and outcomes with the purpose and aims of improving the outcomes and outputs of the education system.
Institute of Space Technology (IST)
has always been in the forefront for accepting and adapting best practices in the field of Education. Recognizing the role that it has to play in higher education sector, IST has established a Quality Enhancement Cell. This cell has the responsibility to ensure that the university’s quality assurance procedures are compatible with international standards and are designed to improve the quality of higher education

Research
Space Systems Lab / Small Satellite Technology & Research Lab
The
Space Systems Lab (SSL)
at Institute of Space Technology serves as a specialized facility for research, development, and hands-on training in small satellite technologies and space systems engineering. The lab supports academic and research activities related to CubeSat development, satellite subsystem design, mission planning, embedded systems, ground segment applications, and space mission operations. It has played a significant role in national space technology initiatives, including the development activities associated with Pakistan’s lunar CubeSat mission ICUBE-Q. The lab provides students and researchers with valuable practical exposure to real-world space engineering challenges, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between computing, electrical engineering, and space science domains while strengthening IST’s contribution to the national space technology ecosystem. The lab was later enhanced under NCGSA and rebranded as
Small Satellite Technology & Research Lab (SSTRL)
.

[H1] Research

Home
Research
Research
The Astronomy Resource Center (
ARC
) has been established at IST to provide scientific data on possibility of
moon-sighting
in various parts of the country on a regular basis and to share information regarding significant astronomical events like solar and lunar eclipse etc. with the public.
IST’s Space Science department is involved in research in various domains of astronomy and astrophysics. These include the following.
Astrophysical Plasmas
: Ionosphere, Solar coronal reheating, galactic magnetic fields, astrophysical jets
Galaxy and black hole mergers
: N-body simulations, gravitational waves from supermassive black holes
High energy astronomy and astrophysics
: Gamma-ray bursts, Active Galactic Nuclei, Atmospheric showers, Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes
Gravitational wave data analysis
: Bayesian inference, Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms, spatial and geostatistics
Extra solar planets and binary stars
: Contact binaries, semi-detached binaries, photometry
Spacecraft environmental interaction
: Spacecraft charging, astrophysical dusty plasma
Experimental plasma techniques
: Plasma thruster, experimental plasma technique, electron cyclotron emission
Researchers at IST are also member of the future gravitational wave detector LISA consortium.
The IST observatory has 10 and 16 inches telescopes used for carrying out observations of various astronomical objects, as well as teaching and demonstration purposes. The observatory also arranges observations of the Moon, planets and other astronomical objects and carries out public outreach activities.

Research
Built to break limits, not just systems.
Positioned at the absolute vanguard of digital defense, the Cyber and Information Security Lab (CISL) is a premier, multi-disciplinary research nexus housed within the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science at the Institute of Space Technology, Islamabad.
We don’t just study the future of cybersecurity - we engineer it.
CISL is powered by a dynamic consortium of elite PhD research fellows and distinguished faculty converging from Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Avionics, and Applied Mathematics. Together, we operate at the intersection of complex mathematics, advanced communications, and information hiding to solve the digital domain’s most critical challenges.

[H1] Research
[H3] Industrial Coating Solutions
[H2] Tribology & Wear Testing

Home
Research
Research
At the Center for Surface Engineering and Tribology (CSET), we provide a comprehensive range of solutions that address industrial challenges in wear, corrosion, performance, and efficiency. Each service is delivered with technical precision, industry insight, and a commitment to cost-effectiveness.
Industrial Coating Solutions
We specialize in advanced coating technologies that extend component lifespan, reduce maintenance downtime, and improve operational reliability.
Capabilities include:
Plasma Spray Coating: High-quality surface protection for critical parts.
High-Velocity Oxy-Fuel (HVOF): Dense, durable coatings with superior wear and corrosion resistance.
Cold Spray Coating: Low-temperature application ideal for repairing sensitive components without thermal damage.
Tribology & Wear Testing
Our tribology laboratory delivers accurate measurement and analysis of friction, wear, and lubrication to help industries enhance material performance and prevent premature failures.
Services include:
Tribometry and wear behavior analysis
Friction coefficient measurement
Lubricant performance testing

[H1] Research
[H3] Advanced Manufacturing Facility

Home
Research
Research
Advanced Manufacturing Facility
From Virtual Concept to Manufactured Product
The Advanced Manufacturing Facility (AMF) at IST is established to provide top quality Precision Manufacturing services for R & D and innovative commercial solutions. The all-inclusive manufacturing setup at AMF boasts top of the line machining equipment, a team of highly trained technical experts, and a holistic design-centric philosophy perfected with experience. AMF complements CAE solutions with Computer Aided Manufacturing (CAM) programs through a well-rounded focus on multi-axis toolpath configuration, collision mitigation, and parameter optimization. Products manufactured at AMF are accurate to 0.001 mm and are thoroughly inspected via CMM before delivery to customers. The machining capabilities of AMF go well beyond what is offered in the market that includes fabrication and processing of hard-to-cut materials such as high-carbon steels, titanium, and nickel alloys. AMF has also installed an automation-based technology by incorporating a robot-actuated Computer Integrated Manufacturing setup that achieves remarkable productivity and accuracy by minimizing human intervention. The complete suite of engineering services provided by AMF include:
5-Axis CNC Machining Center
CNC Turn Mill
Coordinate measuring machine (CMM)
CNC wire-EDM setup
Fixture, Mold, Die Manufacturing
CAD/CAM Services
Design Consultancy

TOPIC  : Avionics System Design Lab
URL    : https://ist.edu.pk/research?section=avionics-system-design-lab

[H1] Research
[H2] Introduction

Home
Research
Research
Introduction
Avionics system design lab is engaged in the design & development of safety critical, complex cyber physical systems. The knowledge base is applicable to all airborne and autonomous systems where safety is paramount.  This Lab serves the dual purpose of practically educating undergraduate avionics engineering students in the advanced concepts of Avionics System Design & conducting research work in the field of Avionics Engineering.
The lab is well equipped to carry out avionics integration work based on Mil-Std-1553B and ARINC-429 data buses. The whole process of the design of certifiable, safety critical avionics systems inclusive of complete System Safety Analysis (in accordance with SAE-4754A/ED-79A & SAE 4761A/ED/84A) and Model Based Design methodology as per RTCA DO-331/ED-218 is demonstrated in the lab. System prototypes comprising software and hardware are developed in line with RTCA DO-178C/ED-12C & RTCA DO-254/ED-80.
The research work is focused both on the spheres of onboard Avionics and CNS+A (Communication, Navigation and Surveillance Avionics) Systems. Key research domains are: -
Flight Control Systems
Autonomous Guidance and Navigation Systems
CNS architectures for Urban Air Mobility
Integration of UAS in National Air Space
Certification of AI/ML in safety critical avionics
Human Machine Interactive Interface

[H2] Business Incubation Center

Home
Research
Research
Business Incubation Center
Business incubation center at the Institute of Space Technology (IST BIC) is working in collaboration with the Higher Education Commission of Pakistan (
www.hec.gov.pk
) to promote technology based business ideas and startups. The management of IST has envisioned the IST BIC as one of the Business Development Services (BDS) provider to serve the local entrepreneurial ecosystem. Companies graduated from the BIC would have the potential to create jobs, revitalize neighborhoods, commercialize new technologies, and strengthen the local and national economies.
The focus of IST BIC is to provide opportunity to the budding entrepreneurs, IST students, faculty and alumni to launch their own startups. The core objective for the establishment of IST BIC is to create a new breed of youth, who believe in their passion and would like to become the job creator rather the job seeker.
We serve our entrepreneurs by providing
Physical and virtual office space.
Co-working space.
Mentoring and coaching.
Qualified / technical faculty.
Utility services.
Commercialization and Marketing support.
PR opportunity.
Access to labs and equipment.
Access to finance and investor connect.
Technical and Business consultancy.
Pre-incubation support

[H1] Research
[H3] Center for Vibration Testing and Condition Monitoring

Home
Research
Research
Center for Vibration Testing and Condition Monitoring
Click to enlarge
Center for Vibration Testing and Conditioning Monitoring (CVCM) provides an opportunity of exploration and revelation in the field of vibrations and acoustics together with solutions to local industry and R&D organizations. The Center is equipped with state-of–the-art equipment for real-time analysis. The structural integrity, durability and strength of different components of machines are analyzed under different loading conditions evading unnecessary machine overhauls. Furthermore, condition monitoring techniques augment machine efficiency and operation time evading expensive equipment damage by continuously monitoring the performance of critical components. CVCM aims towards the prevision of sustainable solutions in critical areas meeting the industrial demands and futuristic needs.
The Vibration Testing and Condition Monitoring (VTCM) have been recognized as a tool promising safety and efficacy in complex parts over the past few decades leading towards innovation and modernization. We, at CVCM, aim comprehensive failure prevention by providing solutions after classifying failure initiation, mode of failure and root causes of failure through vibration testing. For quality ensurance, all the tests are conducted under ISO standard 10816 and 2372. CVCM offers many services as per the significance of vibration diagnostic and control techniques using principals of vibration, signals processing and data acquisition as follows:
Vibration Analysis
Structural Heath Monitoring
Failure and Fracture Analysis
Composite Health Monitoring
Stability
Damping and Isolation Systems
Non-Destructive Testing

TOPIC  : International Conference On Applications Of Space Science
URL    : https://ist.edu.pk/research?section=international-conference-on-applications-of-space-science-&-technology

[H1] Research

Home
Research
Research
Click to enlarge
The International Conference on Applications of Space Science and Technology (ICAST) marks a transformative milestone in Pakistan's journey through space science and technology. As the largest space event in the country, ICAST unites the legacies of IST’s International Conference on Aerospace Science and Engineering (ICASE) and SUPARCO’s International Conference on Space (ICS) into a biennial global forum of unparalleled excellence. ICAST bringing together visionaries, global thought leaders, pioneering researchers, and industry trailblazers, aspires to redefine the future of space science by fostering collaboration, presenting transformative research, and exploring interdisciplinary space applications with the potential to reshape our collective future.

TOPIC  : Journal Of Space Technology
URL    : https://ist.edu.pk/research?section=journal-of-space-technology

[H1] Research
[H2] Spotlights

Home
Research
Research
ISSN 2077-3099 (Print); ISSN 2411-5029 (Online)
Spotlights
Previous editions of JST available for $110 (Complete printed copy)
Journal of Space Technology is an HEC recognized journal (X Category) in which high quality research papers are published in the fields of Aerospace, Communication Engineering and Material Sciences. Subject areas include all the current fields of interest related to the above mentioned categories. Examples include:
Satellite communication, Attitude control, Docking, Satellite tether design
Small Satellites, CubeSats, MIMO in satellite communication
Aerospace, Space craft mission design, Space robotics, Space propulsion
Guidance, Navigation and control, Orbital Mechanics, CFD
On-board computer design, Embedded systems, Hardware programming
Signal analysis, Image processing, Shape and texture analysis
Pattern recognition, Remote sensing, Geographical information systems
Space Environment, Radiation and Environmental effects
Material engineering and sciences, Space materials
Structural design, Thermodynamics
Nonlinear Dynamics & Stability, Data analysis for astronomy and astrophysics
Mathematical Modeling and Simulations, Cryptography, Spatial data analysis
Included papers can cover theoretical research, applied research, experimental results or new insights into previously reported research. To serve the interests of a diverse readership, the introduction should provide a concise summary of the background in an accepted terminology in space technologies, state the unique contributions, and discuss broader impacts of the work outside the immediate subject area. All contributions are reviewed on the basis of scientific merits and breadth of potential interests.

PAGE   : Institute of Space Technology
TOPIC  : Office Of Research, Innovation And Commercialization (Oric)
URL    : https://ist.edu.pk/research?section=office-of-research,-innovation-and-commercialization-(oric)

[H1] Research

Home
Research
Research
The Innovation and Commercialization (I&C) section of our university, in alignment with the guidelines of the Higher Education Commission (HEC) in Pakistan, plays a pivotal role in bridging the gap between academia and industry. Our primary objective is to effectively translate research outcomes into practical applications that contribute to socio-economic development. The I&C section actively promotes research commercialization by identifying commercially viable projects and facilitating their transformation into market-ready products and services. This involves not only the commercialization of ongoing research but also engaging with industry partners to bring innovative projects to exchange mutual expertise and resources.
We place a strong emphasis on supporting startups by providing mentorship, funding opportunities, and incubation facilities, helping to nurture entrepreneurial ventures that emerge from our academic community. Our commitment to intellectual property (IP) management is crucial, as we offer guidance on IP processing and protection, ensuring that our researchers can safeguard their inventions. By building robust industrial partnerships and fostering joint collaborations, we create a dynamic environment that enhances research impact and drives technology transfer.
The I&C section also conducts training sessions and workshops designed to equip students and faculty with the necessary skills for successful entrepreneurship and commercialization. By showcasing our research achievements and success stories, we strive to position the university as a leading hub for innovative solutions that address both national and global challenges, ultimately enhancing our contribution to Pakistan's knowledge economy.

[H1] Research
[H2] Wireless & Signal Processing Lab (WiSP)

Home
Research
Research
Click to enlarge
Wireless & Signal Processing Lab (WiSP)
Wireless & Signal Processing Lab (WiSP) undertakes research projects related to wireless communication, signal and image processing and radio frequency (RF) systems design.
The researchers explore theoretical as well as experimental aspects of wireless communication. Software-defined radios are used to experiment on the PHY and MAC layers of advanced radio technologies including Wi-Fi, LTE, LoRa etc. Machine learning is applied for PHY layer and MIMO processing. Some other research areas include Non-orthogonal waveform, full duplex massive MIMO, context/socially aware wireless networks, optimization in 5G communication, small cell and moving small cell network and D2D communication.
Signal processing research deals with both 1D and 2D signals (images). This includes sparse signal processing, compressive sensing and application of machine learning to acoustic and medical signals, information retrieval and pattern recognition.
The RF stream mainly deals with front-end and antenna design for high altitude platforms and other communication subsystems, such as communication satellites. It also deals with front-end, antenna design and other subsystems for High Altitude Platforms.

Introduction
Physics investigates the laws of nature and is indispensable not only for our understanding of the world but also for the solution of the technological and ecological problems. As a fundamental science, physics continues to be the driving intellectual force in expanding our understanding of the universe, in discovering the scientific basis for new technologies, and in applying these technologies to research.
The Institute of Space Technology has launched a program for BS in Physics, starting from Fall 2020. The BS program in Physics is designed to enlighten students with knowledge from all the vast areas of Physics, including Classical Mechanics, Electrodynamics, Statistical Mechanics, Quantum Mechanics, Particle Physics, Plasma Physics, Condensed Matter Physics, Special and General Relativity etc. Alongside a sound basic education in Physics and Mathematics, BS students would be able to choose attractive, career-oriented study blocks, notably from the fields of Computational Physics, Materials Physics, Environmental Physics, Plasma Physics, High Energy Physics, Electronics and Astronomy & Astrophysics, which is a unique specialization of its kind in Pakistan.
The Department of Physics launched a new program BS Physics with Semiconductors and Chip Design (Minor) in accordance with HEC's new undergraduate education policy.
The Department of Space Science and Physics at IST has distinguished faculty to its credit, who engage in both quality teaching and research. The department's resources not only include the well-trained faculty, but also high-quality labs that provide excellent research opportunities for the students. Active research groups are studying the physics of elementary particles; theoretical and experimental investigations of plasmas ranging from ionosphere to controlled nuclear fusion; electric and magnetic properties of materials; semiconductor physics; astrophysical modeling of supermassive black hole pairs as sources of gravitational waves; observations of stars; study of gamma ray bursts. The students shall be introduced to the research world by working in the diverse fields under the supervision of capable and well-equipped faculty of the department, where emphasis is placed on teaching and research and preparing the students to become the next great physicists of tomorrow and the future to come.
Specializations:
Computational Physics, Materials Physics, Environmental Physics, Plasma Physics, High Energy Physics, Electronics and Astronomy & Astrophysics
Program Educational Objectives
PEO-1:  Demonstrate knowledge of Physics on the fundamental, conceptual and application level.
PEO-2: Ability to comprehend, analyze and address scientific problems in Physics’ domains.
PEO-3: Capacity to work in national or international teams in Physics and ancillary domains, with full professional and ethical responsibilities, and ability to communicate in an effective manner.
Program Learning Outcomes
PLO-1: Scientific KnowledgeKnowledge of the domains of Physics and ability to apply this knowledge to analyze a variety of scientific problems.
PLO-2: Mathematical Skills and KnowledgeSkills in mathematics and comprehension of mathematical concepts needed in Physics.
PLO-3: Modern Tool UsageAbility to use modern tools, techniques and skills to analyze and solve problems in Physics.
PLO-4: Problem AnalysisAbility to identify, formulate, research literature, and investigate scientific problems.
PLO-5: InvestigationAbility to acquire, analyze and interpret data as well as synthesize information to derive valid conclusions.
PLO-6: Environment, Sustainability and SocietyUnderstanding of the impact of Physics in societal and environmental context and knowledge of the needs for sustainable development.
PLO-7: EthicsUnderstanding of ethical principles and an ability to apply them along with a commitment to professional ethics and responsibilities.
PLO-8: Individual and TeamworkAbility to work effectively, as an individual or in a team, in multifaceted and/or multi-disciplinary settings.
PLO-9: CommunicationAbility to communicate effectively, orally as well as in writing with the scientific community and with the society at large.
PLO-10: Project ManagementManagement and leadership skills, to manage projects in a multidisciplinary environment.
PLO-11: Lifelong LearningAbility to recognize importance of life-long learning in the broader context of innovation and scientific developments.

=== DEPARTMENT: Electrical Engineering ===
=== SECTION: Electrical Engineering ===
SOURCE_URL: https://ist.edu.pk/academics?section=electrical-engineering
SCRAPED_AT: 2026-05-18T11:42:56Z

The Department of Electrical Engineering runs an internationally recognized academic program in Electrical Engineering (EE) with different specializations at undergraduate and graduate levels. The department was established in 2002 and started offering a degree in Communication Systems Engineering (CSE). In 2009, keeping in view the expanding focus, the department was renamed as the Electrical Engineering Department. The Department consists of experienced faculty, well-equipped classrooms and state-of-the-art lab facilities. The department provides continuous academic improvement through consultation with faculty, industry, electronics & communication engineering professionals and students. The focus of the courses is on the design, analysis, development and testing of communication & electronic systems encompassing the latest international research trends. The curriculum of Electrical Engineering is designed to provide all-rounder experience to students in fundamental principles and application of electronics, embedded systems, signal analysis, electromagnetic, antennas, digital communications, digital signal processing, image processing, wireless technologies, fibre optics, and satellite systems. The curriculum provides the students a chance to study a variety of courses over the period of four years, and from Fall 2025, the department has also started the BS degree program in Computer Engineering, which has now become one of the most sought-after and premier career choices worldwide.

=== DEPARTMENT: Program Mission Statement ===
=== SECTION: Phd Remote Sensing And Gis ===
SOURCE_URL: https://ist.edu.pk/academics?page=275&section=phd-remote-sensing-and-gis
SCRAPED_AT: 2026-05-18T11:42:56Z

Program Mission Statement
The mission of this program is to develop scientists through quality education and research in the fields of remote sensing and geographical information science. The core scientific goals of this program are to understand the Earth’s physical environment from a geographical and spatial perspective, to advance our knowledge about geophysical processes, and to contribute towards advancing the social and technological applications of space-based and location-based technologies and data. The program will provide its graduates the skills to analyze and interpret remote sensing and geographical data, and the guidance and motivation to address outstanding research questions in the study domain using innovative approaches, both independently and as part of interdisciplinary teams.
Program Educational Objectives (PEOs)
PEO-1: Graduates with a strong theoretical foundation in the concepts of remote sensing and geographical information science, who can utilize the available technological tools to meet the professional needs of academia and industry, and provide solutions on both local and international scales
PEO-2: Graduates with the ability to critically analyze a technical problem and propose innovative solutions for societal benefit
PEO-3: Graduates with the ability to identify a research problem, propose research-based solutions, and be a productive part of research groups in academia or industry
PEO-4: Graduates with knowledge of research ethics, and communication and interpersonal skills to become productive and effective members of interdisciplinary / international teams
PEO-5: Graduates with the motivation and ability to transfer their knowledge, as well as to pursue lifelong learning and continuous improvement of their knowledge and skills.
Program Learning Outcomes (PLOs)
PLO-1: Scientific Knowledge
Attain thorough scientific knowledge in the fields of remote sensing and geographical information science, including fundamental and advanced concepts, and the state of the art in various sub-fields.
PLO-2: Literature Synthesis
Ability to read scientific literature with a critical point of view, and extract relevant information, the ability to evaluate and summarize scientific information from various sources
PLO-3: Problem Analysis and Solution Design
The ability to analyze a research problem, and work towards devising and executing its solution, the recognition and adaption of the scientific method of experiments, results, and analysis
PLO-4: Modern Tool Usage
Knowledge and skills in the modern tools being used in the fields of remote sensing and geographical information science, and the ability to select the best tool for the problem at hand. The ability to learn and design own procedures and algorithms if a solution is not available off-the-shelf.
PLO-5: Interpersonal and Communication Capability
The ability to communicate effectively in oral and written formats, within multi-disciplinary teams and particularly to scientific audiences
Consistency of PEO vs PLO vs Program Mission

Scope of the Program
Whereas the routine RS & GIS applications are being covered by the respective analysts in the field, and the research based products cannot be addressed adequately until PhD level candidates are inducted in the private/public sectors. Even with a fair usage of RS and GIS technologies / datasets, the full benefit of these domains of knowledge has not reached to that level which is required for industry and private sector emerging needs specifically quantitative data analysis and modeling techniques where PhD in Remote Sensing & GIS can play a significant role. The PhD degree in Remote Sensing & GIS can help bring research-based solutions for the private/public sectors in order to compete in the national/international market.
The geoinformation sciences applications are important for a wide range of disciplines including environment, energy sector, agriculture, natural resources management, disaster management, communications etc. The following is a non- exhaustive list of some national-level private and public sector organizations, which could utilize the PhD graduates in remote sensing & geoinformation sciences:
a) Landmark Resources Pvt. Ltd. Islamabad
b) TPL Maps Pvt. Ltd
c) United Nations Development Program
d) Capital Development Authority, Islamabad
e) Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited (PTCL) , Islamabad
f) Pakistan Council of Research in Water Resources (PCRWR), Islamabad
g) Global Change Impact Studies Centre, Islamabad
h) National Agricultural Research Council, Islamabad
i) Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO)
j) National Engineering Services Pakistan (NESPAK)
k) Survey of Pakistan
l) Sui Northern Gas Pipeline Pvt. Ltd.
m) National Highway Authority
n) National Database & Registration Authority (NADRA)
o) Telecommunication Companies
Program Structure and Curriculum
A student has to qualify 8 courses (3 credit hours each) along with 24 credit hours of research thesis and one publication for the award of degree during stipulated time along with the conditions/rules proposed by IST. At least two courses will be offered per semester depending upon the availability of the faculty and requirements of the scholar.
Reference: IST-DEAN-SOP-25/00 (Academic Rules and Regulations for PhD Program) (Annex B)
